From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Sonia Patel <sonia.patel@royalbank.com>
Cc: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.ai>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>, David Kim <david.kim@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 4 Mar 2026 11:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Royal Bank — Redwood evals follow-up & next steps

Hi Sonia (and Rajiv),

Great meeting — glad to see alignment on the two workload slices. Recap + concrete next steps below so we have a single source of truth.

Recap (from our call):
- Workloads: Support summarization & routing (short form ticket -> intent + suggested routing), KYC doc classification (multi-label).
- Success criteria: routing F1 >= 0.82, summarization utility rated >= 4/5 in blinded human eval, classification precision >= 0.9 on critical labels.
- Data: you will provide ~1,000 redacted examples per slice for initial run.

Recommended model candidates (short tradeoffs):
- Mistral-Instruct-7B: low cost, fast latency; good for routing and high-throughput summarization.
- Llama-2-70B (quantized 4-bit): higher quality on nuanced summaries, higher cost/latency; recommended if you need best-in-class summarization quality.
- Redmond-Chat-13B (redwood-verified medium): balanced option — better instruction-following than Mistral, cheaper than unquantized 70B.

(We can run all three as parallel arms in the eval to compare cost/QoE.)

Benchmark & harness links:
- Eval harness + runner: https://github.com/redwood-inference/eval-harness
- Example benchmark report (latency/cost/quality): https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1A2b3Croyalbank-eval-spec

Dataset format (what we need):
- Preferred: CSV with columns: id, prompt, expected_response, task_type, metadata_json.
- For summarization: prompt -> ticket_text, expected_response -> target_summary. For routing: prompt -> ticket_text, expected_response -> intent_label. For KYC: prompt -> document_text, expected_response -> comma-separated labels.
- File name: redwood-eval-template.csv (attached). Please keep PII redacted; a short metadata_json field helps us stratify by channel/region.

Scoring criteria (initial proposal):
- Routing: micro/macro F1 on intent labels; confusion matrix for top-3 intents.
- Summarization: automated ROUGE-L + human pairwise preference (1-5 utility). We'll run a small blinded human eval (n=50) to validate automated metrics.
- KYC: precision/recall per critical label; false-negative analysis for 'do not onboard' labels.

Operational notes for running on Redwood: 
- We will provision a temporary eval space on your Redwood org. For Hosted eval: we'll provide a signed mutual-action-plan + upload creds to a secure S3 folder; alternatively, share a Drive link and we can ingest.
- We support running via our eval runner (see repo) or via a one-off job in the Console; we'll share step-by-step commands once data is uploaded.

Proposed next steps / timeline:
1) You share redacted CSV sample (by EOD Fri 3/6) -> Sonia
2) Redwood provisions eval workspace and baseline runs (3 business days) -> Marissa/Neha
3) Deliver initial report + recommendations (by week of 3/23) -> Marissa

I've attached a Mutual Action Plan (RB-mutual-action-plan-v1.pdf) and a redwood-eval-template.csv with the column examples.

Questions for you now:
- Do you prefer S3 or Drive for data upload?
- Any internal reviewers we should include on the human eval (for privacy/labels)?

I'll loop in Rishi on quantization/latency tradeoffs and David on security/compliance provisioning.

Cheers,
Marissa Cole
Enterprise Solutions
Redwood Inference

Attachments: redwood-eval-template.csv, RB-mutual-action-plan-v1.pdf
